newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch premier sets public debate on airport growth.
newsitem.headline: Dutch premier sets public debate on airport growth.

text.p: The Dutch government aims to launch a public debate on the long-term future of the country's air transport infrastructure early next year, prime minister Wim Kok said on Tuesday.

"There is a real possibility that we will reach (the statutory limits to the growth of Amsterdam's Schiphol airport) sooner than we expected," Kok said. "That is why we need to act with a sense of urgency."
Schiphol's current rate of growth means it is set to reach its statutory maximum of 44 million passengers annually some eight to ten years earlier than 2015, as originally envisaged.
The government has commissioned a study into the future of the aviation infrastructure due for completion in February.

The prime minister's remarks, in a speech to mark the opening of a new World Trade Centre at the airport, were made against the background of growing public opposition to recent sharp increases in air traffic.

Green activists this weekend staged a "balloon protest" in the airport's departures hall to demonstrate against the environmental impact of increased air traffic and plans for a possible second national airport.

Also at the weekend, Schiphol president Hans Smits suggested on Dutch radio a second national airport be built on an artificial island in the North Sea off the coast of IJmuiden. This would solve the problem of aircraft noise, he said.
A spokeswoman for Dutch national carrier KLM, the airport's biggest single user, said the airline would not comment on individual plans.
"We value a central airport with sufficient capacity," she said, adding KLM was not interested in "overflow" airports which would hike costs by fragmenting services.
